items.stem: The buyer of a call option has:

options.text: The right, but not the obligation, to buy the underlying at the strike
options.rationale: Correct: a call grants a right to buy, not an obligation.

options.text: An obligation to buy the underlying at expiry
options.rationale: Buyers hold a right; sellers may have obligations.

options.text: The right to sell the underlying at the strike
options.rationale: That describes a put, not a call.

options.text: A guaranteed profit if the price rises at all
options.rationale: The premium must be recovered before any profit.

items.explanation: Correct: a call grants a right to buy, not an obligation.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which two statements about exchange-traded futures are correct? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: futures are standardised by the exchange.

options.text: They are typically marked to market daily via margin
options.rationale: Correct: daily settlement through margin is standard for futures.

options.text: They are privately customised between two parties

items.explanation: Correct: futures are standardised by the exchange.

items.stem: A long call has a strike of 50 and cost a premium of 3. The underlying is at 52 at expiry. The holder's net result is:

options.rationale: Correct: intrinsic value 2 minus premium 3 is a net loss of 1.

options.text: A loss of the full 3 premium
options.rationale: The 2 of intrinsic value offsets part of the premium.

items.explanation: Correct: intrinsic value 2 minus premium 3 is a net loss of 1.
